claims.claim: A written WotC house style guide exists — 'D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing' v1.04a (©2013), built on Chicago 16 and Merriam-Webster 11 — and it governs typography, numerals, verb collocations, capitalization and tone, with no rule at all on boxed/read-aloud text.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast — D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.04a (©2013; PDF hosted by the Adventurers League blog)
claims.quote: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing

claims.claim: A later revision, v1.08a (©2018, circulated as 'updated January 2019'), keeps the same structure (Chicago 17 now) and adds headings hierarchy, sidebar, gender-suffix, 'fellowship vs party' and edition-naming rules; it still contains nothing on boxed text or read-aloud prose.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast — D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.08a (©2018, 'updated January 2019'; PDF mirror)

claims.claim: The style guide was released publicly on DMs Guild around October 2018 as one of four free PDFs (IP guide, adventure guide, style guide, Forgotten Realms guide) that had previously gone only to official-play writers.
claims.source: EN World — DMsGuild: D&D Style-Guides give a unique insight into the game (thread, 2018-11-25)

claims.claim: On 2019-02-22 the DMs Guild account announced an updated House Style Guide listing for creators, noting it adds tips on gender-neutral language.
claims.source: D&D Sage Advice (sageadvice.eu) — 'Creators: Style Guide is now on DMsGuild!' (@dms_guild, 2019-02-22)
claims.quote: An updated #DnD House Style Guide is now on #DMsGuild

claims.claim: The Kind GM's post on the creator resource carries a May 2020 commenter report that the material was no longer available, which the author acknowledged — so the public window was roughly 2018–2020.
claims.source: The Kind GM — DMs Guild Style Guide Resources (2018-10-24)

claims.feature: house style guide (community says none published)
claims.claim: Community writers on either side of that window report no official guide: Half-Cover (2017) says WotC 'has not yet published the official style guide', Old Dungeon Master (2015) compiled one from 3.5/4e guides ('Perhaps they have one and I just couldn't find it'), and Blog of Holding (2025) says of the 2024 rules 'it annoys me not to have an official style guide'.
claims.source: Half-Cover — How to Follow the Writing Style of D&D (Michael, 2017-09-02)
claims.quote: has not yet published the official style guide

claims.feature: house style guide (community says none published, 2024 rules)
claims.claim: Paul Hughes built an unofficial 2024 style guide because no official one for the 2024 rules is available to the public.
claims.source: Blog of Holding — Unofficial D&D 2024 Style Guide (Paul Hughes, 2025-01-07)
claims.quote: it annoys me not to have an official style guide

claims.claim: Work-for-hire WotC freelancers receive the D&D House Style Guide, the 5e Word template, pitch examples and lore documents at contract start, and drafts are formatted with them.
claims.source: POCGamer — What happened? Writing for Wizards, Part 1 (Graeme Barber, 2021-03-23)

claims.claim: The official Adventurers League Dungeoncraft guide tells authors they must use the provided template and 'formatting standards as presented in the template' and be familiar with the D&D Style Guide, which it says is also provided.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast — D&D Adventurers League Dungeoncraft Design Guide: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight, v1.2 (media.wizards.com)
claims.quote: You should be familiar with the D&D Style Guide

claims.claim: The 2023 Dungeoncraft Design Guide (effective 2023-11-09) again requires a specific template and familiarity with the D&D Style Guide; a poster frames this as organized play needing 'more guiderails than your usual table does'.
claims.source: EN World — D&D Adventurers League Unveils New DungeonCraft Document with Planescape In Focus (Raddu, 2023-11)
claims.quote: more guiderails than your usual table does

claims.claim: Kobold Press ran a 'Designing with Style' series that explicitly 'breaks down the official 5th-edition style guide', quoting its Common Pitfalls section verbatim — evidence the guide was public and treated as canonical by third-party 5e designers.
claims.source: Kobold Press — Designing with Style: Ability Checks and Saving Throws (Hannah Rose, 2019-05-31)
claims.quote: breaks down the official 5th-edition style guide

claims.claim: The guide's stated reason for second person in rules text is gender neutrality: 'In rules text, we often achieve gender neutrality by writing in the second person.'
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast — D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.04a (©2013; PDF hosted by the Adventurers League blog)

claims.claim: v1.04a forbids 'they'/'their' as singular pronouns except in dialogue; v1.08a reverses this 'in a departure from our past usage' but tells writers to rely on it only when no pleasing alternative exists.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast — D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.08a (©2018, 'updated January 2019'; PDF mirror)

claims.claim: The guide fixes the game's verb idiom in a list: you cast a spell, deal damage, make a saving throw that succeeds or fails, make an attack that hits or misses, take damage, regain hit points, score a critical hit, use a feature.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast — D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.04a (©2013; PDF hosted by the Adventurers League blog)
claims.quote: You make a saving throw, and it succeeds or fails

claims.claim: Common Pitfalls: never write 'must make a DC 15 Strength check' unless success and failure are described next; the canonical form is 'must succeed on'.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast — D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.04a (©2013; PDF hosted by the Adventurers League blog)
claims.quote: You must succeed on a DC 15 Strength check

verdicts.trueWording: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing; Version 1.04a ©2013
verdicts.note: Raw PDF fetched (HTTP 200, 9 pp., pypdf extraction). p.1 carries the title verbatim, 'Version 1.04a ©2013 Wizards of the Coast', and the two named foundations: 'The Chicago Manual of Style, 16th edition' and 'Merriam-Webster's Collegiate Dictionary, 11th edition'. Governance limbs all present: typography ('Typographic Treatment of Product Names'), numerals ('Numerals versus Words', 'Numerals in Rules Text'), verb collocations ('Verb Usage', p.6), capitalization ('Terms to Capitalize', p.5), tone (the 'High Fantasy' sidebar: humor/tragedy must not 'overtake the general tone'). Boxed/read-aloud limb confirmed by absence: case-insensitive grep for 'box' = 0 hits and 'aloud' = 0 hits across all 9 pages.

Raw PDF fetched (HTTP 200, 11 pp.). Quote appears verbatim as the opening of the new 'Sidebars' section (p.3). 'Version 1.08a ©2018 Wizards of the Coast' on every page; 'The Chicago Manual of Style, 17th edition' p.1. Additions confirmed against the v1.04a text: 'Headings' hierarchy section (Chapter Title / Heading 1-3 / Inline Subhead), 'Sidebars', 'Gender-Specific Suffixes', and 'Adventuring Parties' — which is the fellowship-vs-party rule ('The word “fellowship” has strong connections with The Lord of the Rings… use “group,” “band,” “company,” or, especially, “party.”'; 'fellowship' = 0 hits in v1.04a). Edition-naming rule is new in wording: 'In a departure from previous usage, we spell out and lowercase references to editions'. Boxed-text limb confirmed by absence: 'box' = 0 hits, 'aloud' = 0 hits. One nuance: 'updated January 2019' is the mirror's filename only — neither 'January' nor '2019' appears anywhere in the document — which matches the claim's own wording 'circulated as'.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: that these PDFs 'had previously gone only to official-play writers' — the EN World thread says nothing about who received them before the DMs Guild posting
verdicts.trueWording: Free on DMsGuild, 'only been on the site a month or so', four PDFs
verdicts.note: Raw thread page 1 fetched (HTTP 200). Remathilis, Nov 25 2018: 'a rather interesting little gem that is free to download: A D&D Style-guide for publishing' and 'Its only been on the site a month or so' — which puts the posting around October 2018 — and 'Its divided into four PDFs: An IP Guide… an Adventure Guide… a Style Guide… and a Forgotten Realms Style Guide'. Those limbs are solid. Greps of the whole page for 'official play', 'organized play', 'Adventurers League', 'previously' and 'only to' return nothing. The missing limb is corroborated verbatim on this chunk's index-53 source (thekindgm.com: 'They were first available only to official play writers but now they're available to the broader public of the DMs Guild') — so the fact is sound but this citation does not carry it.

verdicts.trueWording: An updated #DnD House Style Guide is now on #DMsGuild
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (HTTP 200). The embedded tweet reads verbatim: 'An updated #DnD House Style Guide is now on #DMsGuild, creators! Among other changes, this guide includes tips on achieving gender neutral language.' with the byline '— Dungeon Masters Guild (@dms_guild) February 22, 2019', matching the 2019-02-22 date and the DMs Guild account. The 'listing' limb is also on the page: 'Please note this is a totally new listing! We fixed an error when the original was set up.' (The sageadvice.eu post itself is dated April 1, 2019 — the tweet it archives is 2019-02-22, as the claim states.)

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'so the public window was roughly 2018–2020' — the page never says availability ended; the author's reply is that he fixed the link
verdicts.trueWording: 'Apparently, this material is no longer available.' / 'I have updated the link'
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (HTTP 200). Post dated 'October 24, 2018 May 25, 2020'. Comment by mattwest2342, May 25 2020 5:43 am: 'Apparently, this material is no longer available.' Reply by The Kind GM, May 25 2020 12:33 pm: 'Thank you for bringing it to my attention. I have updated the link'. So the commenter report and the author's acknowledgement are exact. The inference limb is the problem: the author's response points to a working link rather than to a lapse, so this page does not establish that the public window closed around 2020. The page does support the window's opening: 'They were first available only to official play writers but now they're available to the broader public of the DMs Guild.'

verdicts.trueWording: has not yet published the official style guide
verdicts.note: All three sources the sentence names were fetched raw and each quote is word for word. Half-Cover (fetched HTTP 200; page footer '2 Sep 2017 / By: Michael'): 'unfortunately, to my knowledge Wizards of the Coast has not yet published the official style guide for D&D 5th Edition.' Old Dungeon Master (olddungeonmaster.wordpress.com/2015/08/03/5e-writers-guide/, fetched separately HTTP 200, 'Posted by Ronny on August 3, 2015'): 'I was looking for an official writer's guide, or style sheet, from Wizards of the Coast… Perhaps they have one and I just couldn't find it. So I took the copies I had from 3.5 and 4.0 and updated them for 5th edition' — both the quote and the 3.5/4e-compilation limb. Blog of Holding (this chunk's index-55 source, fetched HTTP 200, dated January 7 2025): 'it annoys me not to have an official style guide.' Note for the record that the claim's url field holds only the first of the three; the other two limbs are verified on the pages the sentence itself names, not on half-cover.com.

verdicts.trueWording: it annoys me not to have an official style guide
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (HTTP 200). Full sentence: 'When I'm writing rules for D&D 2024, it annoys me not to have an official style guide. In its absence, I made my own style guide so I can quickly answer my own questions' — quote verbatim, and it carries both the 'built an unofficial 2024 style guide' and the 'because no official one exists' limbs. Title: 'Unofficial D&D 2024 Style Guide (Your Capitalization Questions Answered!)', dated 'Tuesday, January 7th, 2025'. One attribution nuance: the post is first-person and unsigned — 'Hughes' appears nowhere in the page HTML or in the site's RSS feed (no dc:creator tags); the only byline evidence on the page is the sidebar's 'You can also get Paul's DM Notebook', i.e. the first name only.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: that the template is a Word template — the packet list on the page names only 'The 5e Template', never Word
verdicts.trueWording: Receive an instructional packet containing: The D&D Wizards House Style Guide
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (HTTP 200; 'Graeme Barber / 23/03/2021'). Every other limb is exact. Stage 1 is 'Accept the offer, signing an NDA and providing payment information'; stage 2 is 'Receive an instructional packet containing: The D&D Wizards House Style Guide. The 5e Template. An example of a Pitch. Project Instructions. Project Appropriate Lore. An example of a pitch, draft, and extras.' — so style guide, template, pitch examples and lore documents at contract start, all confirmed, in a process the page frames as 'writing for Wizards as a work-for-hire freelance writer'. The formatting limb is verbatim too: 'Drafting Process: You will write a draft, formatted using the Style Guide and Template, and submit it.' Grep for the word 'Word' on the page returns nothing. The Word detail is corroborated elsewhere — the v1.04a style guide (this chunk's index-49 source) says 'If you are using the 5E Template in Word' — but POCGamer does not say it.

verdicts.trueWording: You should be familiar with the D&D Style Guide (also provided) as well.
verdicts.note: Raw PDF fetched from media.wizards.com (HTTP 200, 10 pp.). p.1 'TECHNICAL INFORMATION': 'A template is provided for use, including the Community Created D&D Adventurers League logo. You must use this template, and follow the formatting standards as presented in the template. This logo must appear on your adventure… You should be familiar with the D&D Style Guide (also provided) as well.' Both quoted fragments are verbatim, and 'also provided' carries the claim's final limb. The document self-identifies as 'Dungeoncraft Adventures: The Wild Beyond the Witchlight' for 'D&D Adventurers League' with 'Effective Date: October 1, 2021. Version 1.2.' The same passage repeats for the second option later in the document.

verdicts.trueWording: more guiderails than your usual table does
verdicts.note: Raw thread fetched (HTTP 200; thread starter Raddu, Nov 13 2023). Article body: 'The newly released Dungeoncraft Design Guide, effective from November 9th, 2023, provides comprehensive instructions and standards for crafting these adventures' and 'Creators must use a specific template provided for Dungeoncraft adventures, including the Community Created D&D Adventurers League logo. Familiarity with the D&D Style Guide and adherence to the DMsGuild Content Guidelines are also required.' The forum quote is verbatim in a reply defending the requirements: 'These guidelines above, however, are part of style of play that needs more guiderails than your usual table does', in a post that frames the contrast as Adventurers League / Living campaign play versus a home table — matching 'a poster frames this as organized play'.

verdicts.trueWording: breaks down the official 5th-edition style guide
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (HTTP 200; 'By Hannah Rose / May 31, 2019 / Articles, Designing with Style'). Standfirst verbatim: 'The Designing with Style series breaks down the official 5th-edition style guide to help designers create content that's well-written, polished, and precise.' The Common Pitfalls limb is exact: 'Describing an ability check is so often botched that it falls under the “Common Pitfalls” section of the official D&D House Style Guide (emphasis mine):' followed by a block quote that I diffed against the v1.04a PDF — it reproduces the guide's 'Making a Roll vs. Succeeding on One' paragraph word for word. The trailing clause is the claim's own inference: the page demonstrates canonical treatment by a third-party 5e publisher directly, while 'the guide was public' is inferred from a rival publisher quoting it openly in 2019 rather than stated on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: In rules text, we often achieve gender neutrality by writing in the second person.
verdicts.note: Raw PDF, p.2, under 'Gender' → 'Achieving Gender Neutrality'. The sentence appears exactly as the claim renders it, and it is the guide's only statement about second person, so 'the guide's stated reason for second person in rules text is gender neutrality' is precisely what the page says. (v1.08a softens the same rule to 'we prefer to achieve gender neutrality by writing in the second person whenever possible'.)

Both named versions fetched raw. v1.08a p.2 verbatim: 'In a departure from our past usage, we allow the use of “they” and “their” as singular pronouns, but don't abuse this liberty. Rely on this device only when you have no other reasonable or pleasing alternative.' — giving the quote, the 'in a departure from our past usage' wording and the no-pleasing-alternative limb. The v1.04a limb is verified on the v1.04a PDF (this chunk's index-49 source), p.2: 'Don't use “they” or “their” as singular pronouns, except in an informal context like dialogue.' Slight compression to flag: the older guide's exception is 'an informal context like dialogue', broader than the claim's 'except in dialogue'.

verdicts.trueWording: You make a saving throw, and it succeeds or fails.
verdicts.note: Raw PDF p.6, 'Verb Usage' list. Every collocation in the claim is a line of that list, verbatim: 'You cast a spell.' / 'You deal damage.' / 'You make a saving throw, and it succeeds or fails.' / 'You make an attack (or you attack), and your attack hits or misses (it doesn't succeed or fail).' / 'You take damage.' / 'You regain hit points.' / 'You score a critical hit.' / 'You use a feature.' The list is indeed a fixed list of the game's verb idiom, so the framing limb holds as well.

verdicts.trueWording: You must succeed on a DC 15 Strength check to clamber up the wall.
verdicts.note: Raw PDF p.6, 'Common Pitfalls' → 'Making a Roll vs. Succeeding on One', verbatim: 'Don't mistake making an ability check, a saving throw, or other roll with succeeding on it. The following sentence gets it right: “You must succeed on a DC 15 Strength check to clamber up the wall.” Don't write, “You must make a DC 15 Strength check to clamber up the wall,” unless that sentence is immediately followed by a description of what happens on a success or failure.' Both limbs — the prohibition-unless-consequences-follow and 'must succeed on' as the canonical form — are on the page, in the Common Pitfalls section the claim names.
